item.title: Re: Data not redacted? (Seeking Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
So if i understood right, you wanted to know how all of these ideas will emerge and if they are gonna create a succesful story about all this or not.

-Like why this scp doesnt somehow effect commitee, and why they are refusing to share any information else then not being related to said scp.

-Or another one like why an update after the description says that; now all personal that reads the file needs to take amnestics unless they are ongoing research personal about the said scp while this proposal made by an newly promoted comittee member whos name is blackboxed due to it

-Why the last of the theories about said scp was removed by ethics committee due to possible cognitohazard? Since when ethics comittee are dealing with that?

On a side note to be more specific about theories goes like this: After the initial discovery by junior researcher it goes to collague and his mentor researcher from there they realize something weird or even anomolous goes on. After deciding this researcher goes to site manager and when site manager realizes there is indeed a problem and this effects whole database he/she contacs with one of the O5's to work up with foundation web crawlers.

This all discovery part is created by dialogues between them with some normal kind of explaning.

After the discovery phase, research led by one of the O5's with foundation web crawlers they lay out some theories and any reasons if it can be possible or not like GoI spies. I thought writing them in box style like in SCP-5000 and to the next box reasons of them.

As i mentioned above the last box thingy (dont remember the exact name of it, bracklets?) of theory gets removed by comittee for so called "cognitohazard"

After all these discovery, dialogues between foundation personal and the final conclusion about this being an scp as a result of web crawlers research all these different theories laid on box style.

Also at the end of it with all these minor clues i thought about some part like: You have 1 new message! With collapsibles or something similar with that.

You can like click on the message and someone tells you while showing all the clues in the text if you missed or didnt understand them with the reasonings. He/She tells you that infact this isnt a scp but a committes doing from the start, and gives you explaning why would committee do that.

This mysterious person obviously knows that you are not gonna believe him/her straightforward but gives you more of a "guidance"
to seek truths about all this. He does know that you are currently working for several weeks now on the reason and spread of the said scp and hence knows you dont need to take amnestics, for now.

Maybe this mysterious person is one of the web crawlers? Maybe junior researcher that found it and forced to blackmail by Committee that seeks revenge? Maybe the O5 that started investigations with web crawlers and tries to stay low profile?

But you dont get any more answers, person that wrote you the message wishes you best of luck and finishes his message.

So at the conclusion, reader may find some clues about the Comittee in the file and raise some questions about them but they can also miss or catch all of them too. It depends on viewer perspective at this point i guess. So i tried to make some of them quite obvious while making other ones more secretive in a sense.

And at the end doesnt mattering the result of that if reader catch any clues or not, the twist and story about Committee trying to blackmail/gain upper hand against O5's will be laid out and none of the users will miss it if they press you have 1 message! thing or something similar to that.

-So if user got all clues great for them! They can get satisfacted by the end results

-Lets say user user got some of them and missed the rest, by this the user can go back to reading to check about the other clues in the article about what they missed if they are curious to explore more.

-Or the third option is that, our user missed all of the clues or didnt have any idea about something fishy is going on article. (I really plan to make one of the hints easily understandable just because of this reason) Well maybe they can re-read it from start or read it more carefully because i really think that, it can be should be visible to be understand something weird is going on with this article if read carefully while raising some questions to theories, discovery, amnestics requirement, update by comittee etc.

In option 1 and 2 it can easily lead something is going on but cant tell what it is exactly.
I really hope that this final message sent by mysterious person will be the final delivery and satistaction on theme.
And about option 3 i really think this is unlikely, unless the person didnt read the all story carefully.

On a final sidenote about clues, i am thinking about something like before starting the file; WARNING! BEFORE READING CURRENT FILE UNLESS YOU ARE AN ON-GOING WORK PERSONAL ABOUT SAID SCP, YOU MUST TAKE CLASS-A AMNESTICS AFTER READING.

collapsible YOU MAY ADVANCE

So from the start, even before reading the file they will must know something weird is going on with this SCP

item.title: Re: Data not redacted? (Seeking Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
This feels very reminiscent of stuff like SCP-5242 or Allison Eckhart and I'm sure there's something that plays with the core a lot more closely than either of those; and so I'm left feeling very much like this needs to do a touch more with the idea.

The angle of this being like, the Ethics Committee trying to get the upper hand over the O5's is a pretty good angle and I think it could really help this work but I don't really have a feel for how this article is going to convey that: it's kinda thrown in as a possibility in the hook section; but like, are you going to be somewhat explicit about this? Are you just going to hint towards it? Is it just a possible hypothesis you think a reader might come up with?

I guess at the end of the day, my core question is really: so what are you doing with this? There's like a lot of like, vague hypothesises mentioned in this and they all sound vaguely interesting but I don't really have an idea of how this is all going to come together to form a cohesive article that actually like, tells a story, y'know?

item.title: Re: Data not redacted?
item.content:encoded:

Hence, i wanted to make a more of shorter narrative with some interesting twist and a clue(s) towards that. I thought about what i could add more to this article to make it longer, meaningful or interesting overall.

But then i thought the more detail i add the more ethics comittee involment requires while they can get away with this simple concept without making it overcomplex from back of the foundation. So instead of that i did discovery part by junior, theories made by crawlers and dialogue between researchers.

Maybe i can add some kind of Comittee's efforts to hide it about people who may discover it and giving amnestics to the said people.

But thank you for all critique and will look to add a bit more of a narrative while keeping whole argument not that complicated for Committee's plan.

item.title: Re: Data not redacted?
item.content:encoded:
The narrative is shown primarily through the discovery log, and towards the end it is only implied that it isn't just a GoI but the Ethics Committee. Is this a correct summary?

More crit below!
Oh no!

The narrative of the discovery laid out in the forum is; a junior researcher discovers the anomaly, and brings it to the attention of the senior researcher.

Other than this, there is no other narrative described.

I once was given the crit; "[…]if you don't reveal the story you want to tell, we won't know how to help you!"

I realise that you wish to keep parts of it vague for the readers sake, but at the moment this is an idea concept thread, and its totally ok to reveal these "spoilers"!

My advice is to not worry about spoilers, and reveals, until you have a second or third draft.

We can agree to disagree! Just wanted you to know a little more of my thoughts. I hope this helps!

item.title: Re: Data not redacted?
item.content:encoded:
Thank you for sharing this in IRC!

Crit below!
Geronimo!

The concept reads as familiar. I believe there is an SCP article similar to this concept (my apologies for not remembering the specifics. I believe it was localised to censoring itself though). You can refer to it as a phenomena or object, as an entity it would still be a phenomena.

Part of the hook should be in the central narrative (Ethics Committee essentially black mailing/sabotaging the O5 command).

Your hook is the censorship and corruption itself. In the central narrative, what is the narrative with the GoI and the junior researcher (what I'm asking is not both of them together, but each instance on its own)?

The elevator pitch is a bit long, and as a reader, it’s a giant block of text that I don’t want to engage with. The elevator pitch, in general, is a sales pitch. You; as a writer, are selling us; the readers, on reading the piece- and to engage with the post. Sell us; the readers, on the article. Show us why we should take the time to read it.

I like the hook and concept, but other than that this is lacking too much narrative for me to care as a reader to read the article if it were on the mainlist.

item.title: Data not redacted?
item.content:encoded:
Something or someone is censoring information on foundation database with ████ or [DATA REDACTED] and it is spreading to all known copies including pyhsical ones.

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout: Classic article with table wizard and dialogs

Elevator Pitch: Basic idea is that something is "corrupting" Foundation database with random censors like ████ or [DATA REDACTED] while the censored information was currently known before and cant be find anywhere including any physical copies of it. This phenomenon (due to unknown nature SCP-XXXX supposed to be phenomenon for now) is somehow spreading to other articles.

You may think that hey maybe thats just normal its some kind of error or GoI spies right? First of all we know that it does also censors physical copies of it so it cant be just a simple database error. And for GoI spies, we know that this censor effects both necessary and unnecesaary information so why would GoI spies would take that risk and effort to censor uncessary information or even personal text messages between foundation personal.

Central Narrative: It gives several theories and hypothesis about whats the reason or whats the behind it, is it some sort of entity or GoI spies? Also discovery of it by junior researcher that leads to his senior researcher collague to site director and finally to one of the O5's with the help of foundation web crawlers one by one that shows it has been spread massively over database. However this is just a discovery, initial censor that caused by SCP-XXXX might be the source of its spread but it can also not be and might led to much deeper origins.

Also at the middle of the file (thought about adding this after critique by fairytale) and update comes by a person whos name is blackboxed due to its promotion to being a Comittee Member.(If you want to know why did i explain his name is blackboxed look to hook/attention grabber) This proposal suggests that every person that reads this (Unless they are the on-going working personal on SCP-XXXX) needs to take amnestics due to possible spread might be possible by just having acknowledge about the SCP-XXXX and viewing other files.

+ show block
– hide block

Hook/Attention-Grabber: So we know that somehow SCP-XXXX corrupts database but how we can be sure that SCP-XXXX didnt corrupt this article. (Lets call it Article A) Answer is simple but effective. If there is any censor in article there must be a explanation for it.

For example: Then solution is [DATA REDACTED] (It has been censored due to being possible cognitohazard.)

So by using this method exclusively for our Article A we can be sure that Article A is not corrupted and safe to read.

Secondly in article it says this censor effects everyone except Ethics Comittee. (So including O-5's too.) There are 2 different reasons for it. 1st one is From http://www.scpwiki.com/ethics-committee-orientation/ we know that ethics comittee can read all type of censor hence it doesnt affect them somehow.

2nd reason is much more radical, this scp is nothing but Ethics Comittee doing. Why would they do that? Because they want to gain upper-hand againsts O-5's on power shift between them. They know they are on constant power problem between O-5's and they want to remove it. They know they can censor everything they want and to make it look like SCP they also censor uncessary documents to not draw any attention.
